A name that is declared and never read is clutter at best. Often it points at a bug: a value was computed and then a different name was used, or a refactor left an import behind.

"Used" means read. A variable that is only assigned to or incremented is not used, and neither is a function that only calls itself. Anything you `export` is used.

The rule suggests removing the declaration.

This rule is on by default in JavaScript files. In TypeScript files, `@typescript-eslint/no-unused-vars` is on instead.

## Examples

Reported:

{/* bad {"count": 4} */}
```js
import { readFile, writeFile } from "node:fs/promises";

let saved = 0;

async function save(path, data, options) {
  await writeFile(path, data);
  saved++;
}
```

Not reported:

{/* good */}
```js
import { writeFile } from "node:fs/promises";

let saved = 0;

export async function save(path, data) {
  await writeFile(path, data);
  saved++;
  return saved;
}
```

An unused parameter is only reported if it comes after the last one that is used, because you cannot remove the others:

{/* good */}
```js
export const doubled = items.map((item, index) => index * 2);
```

A component that only appears in JSX is used:

{/* good */}
```jsx
import Button from "./button";

export const App = () => <Button />;
```

## Options

```toml bunfig.toml
[lint.rules]
no-unused-vars = ["error", { argsIgnorePattern = "^_", varsIgnorePattern = "^_" }]
```

| Option | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `vars` | `"all"` | `"local"` skips globals: the names in `/* global */` comments and the top-level variables of a classic script. The top level of a module or a CommonJS file is still checked. |
| `varsIgnorePattern` | none | Regular expression for names of variables that may be unused. |
| `args` | `"after-used"` | `"all"` reports every unused parameter, `"none"` reports none. |
| `argsIgnorePattern` | none | Like `varsIgnorePattern`, for parameters. |
| `caughtErrors` | `"all"` | `"none"` allows an unused `error` in `catch (error)`. |
| `caughtErrorsIgnorePattern` | none | Like `varsIgnorePattern`, for the parameter of `catch`. |
| `destructuredArrayIgnorePattern` | none | Like `varsIgnorePattern`, for names in `const [a, b] = list`. |
| `ignoreRestSiblings` | `false` | Allow unused names next to a `...rest` in object destructuring. |
| `ignoreClassWithStaticInitBlock` | `false` | Allow an unused class that has a `static {}` block, which runs anyway. |
| `ignoreUsingDeclarations` | `false` | Allow unused `using` and `await using` variables, which are disposed of anyway. |
| `reportUsedIgnorePattern` | `false` | Report a name that matches one of the patterns and is used. |

A string in place of the object, `"all"` or `"local"`, sets `vars`.

{/* bad {"options": [{"args": "all"}]} */}
```js
export const doubled = items.map((item, index) => index * 2);
```

{/* good {"options": [{"args": "all", "argsIgnorePattern": "^_"}]} */}
```js
export const doubled = items.map((_item, index) => index * 2);
```

`ignoreRestSiblings` is for taking properties out of an object:

{/* good {"options": [{"ignoreRestSiblings": true}]} */}
```js
const { password, ...publicUser } = user;
send(publicUser);
```

{/* bad {"options": [{"varsIgnorePattern": "^_", "reportUsedIgnorePattern": true}]} */}
```js
const _timeout = 500;
wait(_timeout);
```

By default, a name in a `/* global */` comment that the file never uses is reported too:

{/* bad */}
```js
/* global analytics */

console.log("ready");
```

{/* good {"options": ["local"]} */}
```js
/* global analytics */

console.log("ready");
```
